claims.statement: Vollzeit / Brutto: monthly GROSS income median of full-time employees in Austria, men and women combined, 2024 = EUR 4 317.
Unselbstaendig Erwerbstaetige zusammen / Brutto (headline figure on the page): monthly GROSS income median of all employees in Austria, full-time and part-time combined, 2024 = EUR 3 713.
Vollzeit / Brutto / Maenner: monthly gross median of full-time male employees in Austria, 2024 = EUR 4 517.

assumptions: SOURCE'S OWN: gross monthly income from dependent employment in the main job, including pro-rata holiday and Christmas remuneration, regular overtime compensation, bonuses and commissions; excluding irregular one-off components such as severance payments.
SOURCE'S OWN: full-time/part-time by self-assessment; population = private-household residents excluding parental leave, civil servants and free-service-contract holders.
THIS IS A GROSS FIGURE. It is before all social insurance contributions and before wage tax. It must NOT be used for a cost-vs-salary break-even calculation.
notes: *** THIS IS GROSS, NOT NET. *** EUR 4 317 is what a full-time Austrian employee earns before the state takes anything. For the corresponding take-home figure use artifact 010_net_monthly_income.json (EUR 3 084). The two figures come from the same table on the same page, so the published-implied relationship at the median is roughly 4 317 gross -> 3 084 net for the same population, i.e. the official net/gross ratio at the median is about 71.4 per cent - but note this is a ratio of two MEDIANS of different sub-populations' underlying withholding situations, NOT an individual effective tax rate, and it must not be reused as a general 'net = x% of gross' conversion rule for other countries or other incomes. Currency EUR, reference year 2024.
evidence_limitations: All employees, not graduates. Same population caveats as artifact 010. Included here only so the corpus can see the official gross counterpart to the official net median and can sanity-check that a gross figure has not been mistaken for a net one.
